title: On‑Prem vs VPC Tradeoffs: Licensing & Bundle Sensitivity (working sheet)
body:
PURPOSE:
Quick working TCO + ROI table and sensitivity sweeps for on‑prem vs VPC for mid-market customers. Focus: licensing and support bundle packaging levers that change payback and 3‑year TCO. NOT a final proposal — this is a modeling scratchpad for pricing conversations and solutions engineering handoff.

KEY ASSUMPTIONS (baseline):
- Workload: steady-state 500 qps equivalent bursts to 2k qps; avg seq len 64 tokens; 1M monthly active inference sessions (~tokens normalized).
- Utilization: baseline on‑prem GPU utilization 65% (engine amortized across batch/steady). VPC reserved utilization assumed 55% (includes cloud idle).
- HW amortization: 3 years straight line. Servers include 8xA100/80GB equivalent per rack.
- License model (baseline): on‑prem perpetual model: $X per GPU (capex-adj) + annual support % of license. VPC model: subscription monthly per inference-unit with included basic support; enterprise bundle options for premium support, on-call, and faster SLA.
- Support tiers: Basic (email, 48h SLA), Business (phone, 8h), Enterprise (onsite/white glove, dedicated CSE, 2h).

SCENARIO SUMMARY (high level rows — year 1 and total 3yr):
Columns: Scenario | GPUs | Capex (HW + infra) | Licenses Y1 | Support Y1 | Cloud/Opex Y1 | Total Y1 | Total 3yr (amortized + recurring) | Payback (months) | Notes

Row: On‑Prem Heavy | 48 GPUs | $1,420,000 | $240,000 | $150,000 | $60,000 ops | $1,870,000 | $2,430,000 | 22 | Best unit cost if utilization >70%, higher upfront
Row: VPC Hosted (reserved + burst) | equivalent perf | $0 | $560,000 (subscription conv.) | $72,000 | $440,000 cloud | $1,072,000 | $3,216,000 | 8 | Lower upfront, higher 3yr run cost, easier for PLG growth
Row: Hybrid (dedicated reserved + on‑prem edge) | 32 GPUs (core) + cloud buffer | $980,000 | $360,000 | $110,000 | $220,000 | $1,670,000 | $2,050,000 | 14 | Good middle ground — recommended for regulated customers with seasonal peaks

NOTES ON CALCS:
- Capex includes servers, bare-metal switches, racking, initial NOC setup (one‑time).
- Cloud/Opex line for VPC includes reserved capacity commit amortized + burst overlay cost at projected 30% additional spend.
- License Y1 for VPC reflects annualized equivalent of our subscription price × expected consumption.
- Total 3yr includes 3× annual recurring (licenses/support/cloud) + amortized HW for on‑prem/hybrid.

SENSITIVITY SWEEPS (quick outputs):
1) +10% GPU list price (affects on‑prem capex): On‑Prem Total 3yr +$140k (≈+5.8%). VPC unaffected.
2) -15% utilization (on‑prem): Unit cost +12% and payback pushes +6 months.
3) Support upsell (move 20% of customers to Enterprise tier): Incremental support rev +$180k/year, negligible effect on HW capex but improves revenue/CS SLA margin.
4) License discount trigger: 20% volume discount threshold at commit >$1.2M/yr — lowers VPC effective subscription to near parity with on‑prem at 3yr for enterprise deals.

DETAILED SENSITIVITY TABLE (cells as narrative rows — engineers: convert into sheet formulas):
- Variable: GPU price | Baseline $29.6k/GPU-equivalent | Range tested: -20% / +20% | Impact: changes Capex, amortization, and per-inference unit cost.
- Variable: Utilization | Baseline 65% | Range tested: 40%–85% | Impact: biggest driver of on‑prem unit economics.
- Variable: License effective rate | Baseline on‑prem $5k/GPU/year support + $5k/GPU perpetual license amortized | VPC baseline $46k/year subscription (scaled) | Impact: shifts 3yr parity point.

RECOMMENDATIONS (working):
- Bundle strategy: 3 canonical bundles for sales to offer (names for conversation):
  1) CoreShield (On‑prem lite): low up‑front license, 3yr amortized HW financing option, Business support included. Target: regulated mid‑market.
  2) FlexReserve (Hybrid): moderate capex + VPC buffer, Enterprise support optional. Target: growth SaaS customers with predictable peaks.
  3) CloudStarter (VPC subscription): zero capex, monthly subscription with tiered commit discount; include option to buy-down into CoreShield after 12 months. Target: PLG & startups.
- Pricing levers and negotiation playbook:
  - Give license volume discounts at >$500k ARR threshold in return for 18–24 month committed usage and a signed support SLA.
  - Trade larger upfront license for lower annual support % to improve sales NRR friendliness.
  - Offer cloud-to-onprem buy-down credit (apply 60% of first‑year subscription to HW/license purchase if customer moves to on‑prem within 18 months).

REVENUE & OPS IMPACTS (notes):
- Upsell path: customers starting on CloudStarter should be targeted at month 9–12 for commit conversation to FlexReserve or CoreShield. Revenue recognition and cash collection differ; PS involvement required for CoreShield installs.
- Cost to serve: Enterprise support adds ~0.8 FTE of CSE per 12 large enterprise customers; include that in margin model.

SALES ENABLEMENT NOTES (to include in playbook):
- One‑page sheet for AE: "Which bundle to propose" decision tree (regulatory / growth / budget).
- Checkbox for privacy requirements: if customer requires KMS/HSM + SOC2 HIPAA info, recommend CoreShield or Hybrid.
- Template discount matrix: show list price, 10% early commit, 20% >=$1.2M, bespoke for >$3M.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs (working list):
- [ ] Validate baseline utilization with Solutions Eng telemetry (ask SRE to export 6 months of GPU utilization by customer segment) — jira PD-3421 assigned to Diego.
- [ ] Reconcile license amortization assumptions with finance (tax treatment, financing offers) — finance owner Priya.
- [ ] Build a canonical spreadsheet version with scenario toggles and formula fields (owner: Alyssa) — convert this sheet into PROD model.
- [ ] Add token-level unit economics mapping (tokens → GPU-minutes → currency) for more granular pricing.

REFERENCES & LINKS: (see linked_artifacts above)
- Confluence design doc: PD-arch-2024-onprem-vpc (arch diagrams, infra assumptions)
- Jira: PD-3421 (utilization export), PD-3488 (bundle naming and legal term draft)
- GitHub: infra PR#981 (cost model template for on‑prem amortization)

QUICK TALKING POINTS FOR CSM/AE:
- "If you want the lowest long‑term unit cost and you can commit to >70% utilization, on‑prem CoreShield is our most economical path. If you need fast time‑to‑value and low cash‑burn, start with CloudStarter and convert at month 12 for credits. Hybrid is the pragmatic compromise for regulated customers with seasonal load spikes."

NEXT STEPS (1–3 weeks):
1) Build canonical sheet with formula cells and toggles (owner: Alyssa).
2) Run sensitivity automated sweep across utilization 40–85% and GPU price ±20% to produce break‑even heatmap (owner: Diego).
3) Draft sales one‑pager and AE decision tree and route for legal review for discount triggers (owner: Priya).

DOCUMENT HISTORY / NOTES TO SELF:
- Iteration 1: initial numbers based on infra benchmarks and past deals (Oct 2024).
- Iteration 2: updated VPC pricing with new reserved pricing (Dec 2024).
- Iteration 3: added hybrid scenario and recommendations (Feb 2025).

-END OF WORKING SHEET-"
